name: Yahoo Finance market data
statement: DRAFT FOR SIGNATURE — NOT SIGNED. The signer is asked to approve NOTHING for yahoo_finance. permitted_uses is empty by finding, not by omission, and this draft recommends REFUSAL plus replacement of the source. APPROVED: nothing. NOT APPROVED, each for a clause actually read: (a) redistribute_raw — 'Ownership and Reuse' forbids reproducing, distributing or transmitting any portion of the Services absent explicit written permission, which IGRM does not hold; (b) publish_extract — a published price extract is that same reproduction at record level; (c) cite_metadata — in this project's vocabulary cite_metadata means publishing per-record fields, and for a price series the record IS the licensed content, so it collapses into (b); (d) model_processing — the acquisition step itself is unpermitted, so no downstream computation can be bootstrapped from it: 'Member conduct' bars collecting data 'using any automated means ... including but not limited to robots, spiders, scrapers, data mining tools, or data gathering or extraction tools, for any purpose without our express, prior permission', and src/fetch_markets.py does exactly that through yfinance. ALSO EXPLICITLY NOT APPROVED, though it is not a value in this schema's vocabulary: publication of derived statistics computed from Yahoo prices (publish_derived_value in the repo's own vocabulary). The 'Ownership and Reuse' prohibition on 'create derivative works based on' is not conditioned on commercial purpose, so the project's standing 'used but never redistributed' discipline does not by itself reach it — and eight docs/data payloads carrying Yahoo-derived numbers, event_study.json and sector_sensitivity.json among them, are stamped CC BY 4.0, which purports to grant downstream users redistribution and commercial reuse that Yahoo has not granted IGRM. max_current_age_days is null because no lane is approved, so there is no freshness window to authorise. No permission is inferred from Yahoo Finance being publicly viewable, from the yfinance library existing, or from the data being 'only market context': the yfinance maintainer states the library is 'not affiliated, endorsed, or vetted by Yahoo, Inc.' and that the endpoint 'is intended for personal use only'. The signer's real choice is (a) obtain written permission or a licensed feed from Yahoo or a vendor, (b) replace the source with one whose terms permit the derived publication IGRM actually performs — official NSE/BSE index series, RBI reference rates for USDINR, a licensed vendor — or (c) retire the market-context lane under the project's retirement policy (30-day changelog notice, tombstone). This draft recommends (b), with (c) as the fail-closed default if (b) is not in place before the next publication of Yahoo-derived numbers.

_draft_only.status: UNSIGNED DRAFT - not valid authority until signed
_draft_only.verifier_note: I independently fetched https://legal.yahoo.com/us/en/yahoo/terms/otos/index.html and confirmed the draft's four operative clauses verbatim; I did not rely on the draft's reading. No overclaim is structurally possible here because permitted_uses is [] - the draft asserts zero authority, so no drafted permission can exceed what the terms grant. Confidence 'terms_read_directly' is justified: the document is reachable and the quotations are accurate. Clause support for refusing each lane: (a) redistribute_raw and (b) publish_extract are barred by Sec 2.8 'Ownership and Reuse' ('Unless you have explicit written permission, you must not reproduce, modify, rent, lease, sell, trade, distribute, transmit, broadcast, publicly perform, create derivative works based on, or exploit for any commercial purposes, any portion or use of, or access to, the Services'), and IGRM holds no such written permission; (c) cite_metadata correctly collapses into publish_extract because docs/codebook.md:446 confirms cite_metadata is a genuine record-level publication lane in this project's vocabulary (used alongside publish_extract for GDELT record fields), and for a price series the record IS the licensed con
_draft_only.unresolved_for_founder: FOUR items the founder must decide personally; none can be closed from the terms text alone. (1) THE CC BY 4.0 CONFLICT — the sharpest one. Eight payloads under docs/data/ carrying Yahoo-derived numbers (api_contract, aptness, event_study, receipts, receipts_archive, sector_sensitivity, spike_breadth, status) are stamped 'license':'CC BY 4.0' in _meta. That stamp offers downstream commercial redistribution of derivative works built on data Yahoo's terms say may not be used to create derivative works without explicit written permission. Decide whether to carve the Yahoo-derived fields out of the CC BY 4.0 grant, drop those fields, or replace the upstream source. This is a publication-surface decision, not a fetch decision, and it is live today. (2) COMMERCIAL CHARACTER OF IGRM — 'you may not access or reuse the Services ... for any commercial purpose' turns on whether igrm.in, a free public index published by an independent researcher that nonetheless offers a permissively licensed API and carries the founder's professional identity, is a commercial purpose. I am not a lawyer and did not guess; a qualified Indian-law opinion should settle it before any approval is signed. (3) JURISDICTION AND ENTITY — the terms I read are the /us/en/ text. The India (in) region block names Yahoo India Private Limited only for Yahoo Mail and Yahoo Search; Yahoo Finance is named as provided by Yahoo Finance LLC. Confirm which entity, governing law and forum actually bind an India-resident user of Yahoo Finance, and re-read the terms served to an Indian IP if that differs. (4) RETROSPECTIVE EXPOSURE — Yahoo-derived numbers are already published and already in git history and in any archive mirror. Decide whether a corrections-ledger entry and a retraction or relicensing of the affected fields is warranted, or whether forward-only remediation is enough. Related smaller item: data/raw/prices.csv is gitignored and the frozen-cache path in fetch_markets.py is correct discipline, but confirm no market cache has ever been committed or shipped in a release bundle before relying on that. Nothing in this draft should be signed until (1) and (2) are answered.
